candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

types.embedding_query_text: Population: The number of people living in a place. Also called inhabitants, residents. Examples: 66,000 people.

chosen_type.label: Population
chosen_type.definition: The number of people living in a place.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for population count; 66,000 people is a population.

candidates.label: Residence
candidates.comment: A Residence is a Place where a person lives. Also called home, dwelling, abode. Examples: a house, an apartment, a condominium, a dormitory room.

candidates.label: StatisticalPopulation
candidates.comment: A set of instances of a given type that satisfy specific constraints, used for statistical analysis. Also called statistical group, data population, sample group, target demographic. Examples: all persons with a home location in a specific city, all events occurring in a particular year, all news articles mentioning a certain keyword. Distinct from StatisticalVariable, which represents a measurable metric within a population.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A proportion expressed as a fraction of 100. Also called proportion, share. Examples: 25%, 31%, 69%.

chosen_type.label: Number
chosen_type.justification: 25%, 31%, 69% are numeric values.

candidates.label: Float
candidates.comment: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValueDistribution
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValueDistribution is a StructuredValue representing a statistical distribution of values. Also called value distribution, statistical range. Examples: the average height of a population with standard deviation, a product's price distribution across different retailers, a range of test scores with median and mode.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

types.embedding_query_text: Group: A set of people or things considered together. Also called set, collection. Examples: four people, 11 people, three people, two people.

chosen_type.label: Collection
chosen_type.definition: The act of gathering items or data for a specific purpose.
chosen_type.justification: Groups of people (four people, 11 people) are collections.

candidates.label: Collection
candidates.comment: A grouping of various items, which can include creative works or products. Also called assortment, compilation, set, aggregate. Examples: A collection of rare books, a stamp collection, a music album, a product catalog.

candidates.label: Series
candidates.comment: A general group of related items, which may or may not be of the same kind, forming a sequence or collection. Also called collection, sequence, set, installment. Examples: a book series, a lecture series, a product line, a collection of artworks. Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is a series of creative works.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: ProductGroup
candidates.comment: A ProductGroup is a Product representing a group of products that vary only in specific attributes like size, color, or material, serving as a template for its variants. Also called product family, product line, variant group. Examples: a specific model of smartphone available in different colors and storage sizes, a t-shirt design available in various sizes and fabrics, a car model with different trim levels. Distinct from Product, which is a specific variant offered for sale.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

types.embedding_query_text: Ship: A large watercraft. Also called vessel, boat. Examples: two dry cargo ships, shadow fleet vessels, tankers.

chosen_type.label: Vehicle
chosen_type.justification: Ships are vehicles.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: Canal
candidates.comment: An artificial waterway constructed for navigation, irrigation, or drainage. Also called waterway, artificial channel, navigation channel. Examples: Panama Canal, Suez Canal, Erie Canal, Grand Canal of China.

candidates.label: Car
candidates.comment: A wheeled, self-powered motor vehicle primarily used for personal transportation. Also called automobile, motorcar, auto, vehicle. Examples: Toyota Camry, Ford F-150, Tesla Model 3, Honda Civic.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryVessel: A ship used for military purposes. Also called warship, naval craft. Examples: two military patrol boats, patrol boats.

chosen_type.label: MilitaryVessel
chosen_type.definition: A ship used for military purposes.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for military vessels; patrol boats are military vessels.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: BoatTerminal
candidates.comment: A CivicStructure serving as a station for boats, ships, and other water vessels to dock and embark/disembark passengers or cargo. Also called ferry terminal, cruise port, marina, dock. Examples: "The Seattle Ferry Terminal", "PortMiami cruise terminal", "A local marina office".

candidates.label: LymphaticVessel
candidates.comment: A type of vessel within the anatomical structure of the body that specifically carries lymph fluid towards the heart. Also called lymph vessel, lymphatic duct, lymphangion. Examples: thoracic duct, right lymphatic duct, lacteal. Distinct from BloodVessel, which carries blood.

candidates.label: BoatReservation
candidates.comment: A Reservation for travel on a boat, ship, or other water vessel. Also called ferry booking, cruise reservation, boat charter booking. Examples: "A reservation for the Staten Island Ferry", "A booking for a private yacht charter", "A cruise cabin reservation". Distinct from BoatTrip, which describes the journey itself.

candidates.label: BoatTrip
candidates.comment: A Trip representing a journey taken on a commercial ferry line or similar water transport. Also called ferry journey, boat excursion, water travel. Examples: "A ferry trip across the English Channel", "A sightseeing boat trip on the river", "A commercial fishing boat trip". Distinct from BoatReservation, which is the booking for the trip.

types.embedding_query_text: Revenue: Income, especially from taxes or sales. Also called income, earnings. Examples: oil revenues.

chosen_type.label: Revenue
chosen_type.definition: Income, especially from taxes or sales.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for revenue; oil revenues are income.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

candidates.label: MerchantReturnPolicy
candidates.comment: An intangible providing information about product return policies associated with an organization, product, or offer. Also called return policy, refund policy, merchandise return terms. Examples: "30-day return policy", "final sale policy", "return policy for electronics".

candidates.label: Energy
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Energy represents a numerical value combined with a unit of energy. Also called power, work, heat. Examples: "100 kWh", "500 Joules", "200 Calories", "1.21 Gigawatts".

candidates.label: MerchantReturnEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of various kinds of product return policies offered by merchants. Also called return policy type, refund option, merchandise return category. Examples: "NoReturns", "FreeReturns", "ReturnsWithFee", "ExchangeOnly".

candidates.label: PaymentStatusType
candidates.comment: PaymentStatusType is an enumeration for specific payment statuses. Also called payment state, transaction status, billing status. Examples: PaymentDue, PaymentComplete, PaymentDeclined, PaymentFailed. Distinct from OrderStatus, which describes the overall order state.

types.embedding_query_text: Conflict: A serious disagreement or armed struggle. Also called war, hostilities. Examples: war, full-scale invasion.

chosen_type.label: Negotiation
chosen_type.definition: A discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for conflict; war is a conflict event.

candidates.label: DisagreeAction
candidates.comment: A react action expressing a negative opinion or difference of opinion regarding an object, proposition, or theme. Also called Express disagreement, object to, dispute, dissent. Examples: Disagreeing with a political statement, objecting to a proposed plan, disputing a fact. Distinct from AgreeAction, which expresses positive sentiment or agreement.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Infrastructure: The basic physical systems of a country or region. Also called facilities, installations. Examples: fuel, energy and transport facilities, critical infrastructure facility, energy facilities, transport facilities.

chosen_type.label: Infrastructure
chosen_type.definition: The basic physical systems of a country or region.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for infrastructure; fuel, energy, transport facilities are infrastructure.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

types.embedding_query_text: MilitaryFacility: A site used for military operations or storage. Also called base, installation. Examples: drone storage sites.

chosen_type.label: DefenceEstablishment
chosen_type.justification: Drone storage sites are military facilities, matching DefenceEstablishment.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: ParkingFacility
candidates.comment: A ParkingFacility is a civic structure providing space for parking vehicles. Also called parking lot, parking garage, car park. Examples: a multi-story parking garage, a supermarket parking lot, a valet parking service. Distinct from Road, which is for vehicle travel.

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: SingleFamilyResidence
candidates.comment: A type of house designed to be occupied by one family, typically detached from other homes. Also called detached house, single-family home, private residence. Examples: a suburban house with a yard, a standalone cottage, a bungalow.

candidates.label: Airport
candidates.comment: An Airport is a CivicStructure that serves as a facility for aircraft to take off and land, and for passenger and cargo services. Also called airfield, aerodrome, air terminal. Examples: London Heathrow Airport, John F. Kennedy International Airport, Tokyo Narita Airport. Distinct from Airline, which is the company operating flights.

types.embedding_query_text: Equipment: Tools or supplies needed for a purpose. Also called supplies, gear. Examples: generators and backup supplies.

chosen_type.label: Equipment
chosen_type.definition: Tools or supplies needed for a purpose.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for general equipment; generators and backup supplies are equipment.

candidates.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
candidates.comment: An OfficeEquipmentStore is a local business that sells supplies and equipment for offices. Also called office supply store, stationery shop, business equipment retailer. Examples: Staples, Office Depot, a local stationery shop. Distinct from ComputerStore, which specializes in computers.

candidates.label: Vehicle
candidates.comment: A device designed or used for transporting people or cargo across various environments. Also called conveyance, transport, automobile. Examples: a car, a bicycle, an airplane, a boat, a truck.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

candidates.label: HowToTool
candidates.comment: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

candidates.label: MedicalDevicePurpose
candidates.comment: An enumeration of categories for medical devices, organized by their purpose or intended use. Also called device use, medical equipment function, intended purpose. Examples: "Diagnostic", "Therapeutic", "Surgical", "Monitoring".

types.embedding_query_text: Border Examples: Ukrainian border.

chosen_type.label: Border
chosen_type.definition: A boundary line separating two areas.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for border; Ukrainian border is a boundary.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: GeoCircle
candidates.comment: A GeoCircle is a GeoShape representing a circular geographic area, defined by a center point and a radius. Also called circular region, geographic circle. Examples: A 5-mile radius around a city center, a circular search area defined by latitude/longitude and radius, a geofence for a specific location.

candidates.label: GeoShape
candidates.comment: A GeoShape is a StructuredValue representing the geographic shape of a place, described using latitude/longitude pairs. Also called geographic area, spatial boundary, region. Examples: A polygon defining a city boundary, a circle representing a search radius, a line segment for a road.

candidates.label: GatedResidenceCommunity
candidates.comment: A GatedResidenceCommunity is a Residence type that is a residential area with restricted access. Also called gated community, private estate. Examples: A luxury residential complex with controlled entry, a retirement community with security gates, a private housing development.

candidates.label: Map
candidates.comment: A creative work that visually represents an area, showing features like roads, cities, or terrain. Also called cartographic representation, geographical chart, atlas page. Examples: a road map, a topographic map, a subway map, a world atlas.
